preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the shutter-instant auto-gate and the confirm-or-override-with-written-justification mandate verbatim; they collapse the operator's at-the-moment judgment into a traceable annotation step. The concrete design choice I advance: a hard four-week maximum-suspension cap on the decoupled tally clock, after which a mandatory physical inspection of the implicated sensor occurs and, if drift is confirmed, that sensor's auto-gate is disabled for the remainder of the reverification window while the frame falls back to operator visual assessment annotated "SENSOR-DRIFT OVERRIDE — CAL-CERT DATE [X] — RUNNING Δ [Y mm/h]," so the appendix reader distinguishes a drift-induced hold from a true weather-induced one by reading the certificate date against the drift-trend delta. The failure this cap and override expose: Site 1, week 6, the housing-embedded condensation sensor creeps +0.3 mm/h/week—individually below the single-sensor ambiguous threshold—yet the composite OR-gate (condensation ∨ precipitation ∨ visibility) trips on condensation alone every Tuesday, the four-week cap expires at week 10, inspection confirms the creep, and the operator overrides frames for weeks 7 through 10 to "present" from hurried visual truck sightings while the drizzle persists. Those four override frames carry empty truck-identification fields because the technician was rushing to complete the pressure reading before the drizzle intensified, so a year-three appendix reader sees four "present" annotations with blank identification cells and cannot determine whether the transient genuinely appeared or the operator was pattern-matching a grey blur. I therefore mandate that any frame generated under a sensor-drift override must include a second-observer photograph taken from a fixed 30-metre offset tripod within ninety seconds of the shutter instant, logged as a cross-reference pair in the decouled subsection, so that identification metadata is captured independently of the primary operator's time pressure.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the second-observer cross-reference pair and the ninety-second co-shutter mandate verbatim; they strip the primary operator's schedule pressure out of the identification-metadata cell. The concrete design choice I advance: the thirty-metre offset tripod is permanently fixed at a published azimuth and elevation that renders the two frames geometrically registerable, and if the precipitation-rate delta between the two shutter instants exceeds 1.5 mm/h the pair is auto-annotated "TEMPORAL STATE DIVERGENCE — NEITHER FRAME VALID" and quarantined, so no operator can force-match them under interval pressure. The failure this closes: week 12, Site 2, a convective burst delivers four mm/h in the first thirty seconds then clears; the primary shutter at t-zero catches heavy rain, the offset tripod at t + 85 s catches clear sky, and the technician—rushing to complete the pressure reading before the next interval—force-logs the pair as present/present with blank identification cells; the year-three appendix reader sees two photographically contradictory frames stamped as a matched pair and cannot distinguish a thirty-second convective drop from a sustained transient unless the quarantine annotation, carrying its paired precipitation deltas, separates the pair from a legitimate co-occurring observation.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the fixed-azimuth quarantine annotation with its paired precipitation deltas verbatim; it makes the thirty-second convective divergence visually separable from a sustained co-occurring transient in any year-three appendix read. The concrete design choice I advance: before the 1.5 mm/h threshold comparison, the system subtracts each gauge's last-certificate-to-present drift (tracked from the calibration log at every weekly certificate renewal) so the delta tests true spatial-temporal divergence rather than instrument error, and if the residual inter-gauge calibration uncertainty after subtraction exceeds 0.5 mm/h the quarantine annotation is replaced with "CAL-UNCERTAINTY DOMINANT — QUARANTINE SUPPRESSED — FRAME CLASSIFIED BY PRIMARY OPERATOR VISUAL ONLY, OFFSET FRAME ARCHIVED UNMATCHED," waiving the cross-reference obligation for that interval. The failure this subtraction and suppression rule closes: week 21, Site 2, the offset-tripod gauge has drifted +0.6 mm/h since its week-14 certificate while the primary gauge (week-2 certificate) holds, so a genuine 1.0 mm/h convective-spatial delta is recorded as 1.6 mm/h, trips the quarantine, and accumulates into an 18% weekly quarantine rate that exceeds the hypothetical 12% site-repositioning review threshold, sending an unnecessary survey crew to a geometry-adequate site while the real drift goes uncorrected because no annotation ever flagged the calibration state as the causal variable. The suppression annotation, carrying both certificate dates and the computed drift vector, lets the appendix reader reconstruct that the quarantine was an artifact and retroactively re-admit the offset frame into the decouled subsection under the primary operator's visual classification, preserving the convective transient's record without altering the site's geometry or the operator's interval schedule.
